The new construction turns a short response experiment into a collective fermionic loading operation, with a guarantee on every specified cluster of vacancies. It handles an unknown Hamiltonian within an explicit physical class and uses finite-quality, finite-rate particle supply.

The useful target changed during the investigation. If destructive particle detection already clears reusable modes, preparing empty modes adds little. I therefore constructed the corresponding particle-loading operation: deliver occupied modes, with vacancies as the errors. This requires a real occupied reservoir; particle–hole notation does not manufacture that resource.

The enabling principle

The starting representation uses established passive fermionic Gaussian and linear-Lindblad machinery. The new local derivations connect that representation to worst-case initialization and a controller learned from a scalar response.
